metadata.scenario: A nurse calls the office from a patient's home to report that she completed the morning visit and the patient's vitals are stable. She asks if there are any schedule changes for the afternoon. Quick staff coordination call.

transcription.text: CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Lucille Davis. I just had a nurse here for my morning visit. Hi Lucille! I hope everything went well. What did the nurse report? She said my vitals are stable, which is good. I wanted to check if there are any changes to my afternoon schedule. Let me look that up for you. One moment please. Okay, I see that your afternoon visit is scheduled as usual. Is there anything specific you need to discuss? Not really, but I wanted to confirm if the same nurse will be coming back. I can check that for you. If you give me a moment... Yes, it looks like Sarah will be coming back this afternoon. She’s familiar with your care routine. That’s great! I feel comfortable with her. I’m glad to hear that. Just a reminder, if you have any changes to your condition, please let her know. Absolutely, I will. And Lucille, have you thought about getting some physical therapy sessions? Hmm, I haven’t really considered it. What does that involve? Our physical therapy service focuses on mobility training and improving strength. It’s $110 to $140 per session. That sounds interesting, but I’m not sure I can afford that right now. I understand, but we can help with insurance authorization if you’d like. Oh, that would be helpful! I’d like to explore that option. Great! I’ll have Lisa, our Care Coordinator, give you a call to discuss the details. Thank you, I appreciate that. You’re welcome! Is there anything else I can assist you with today? No, that covers it. I’ll look forward to hearing from Lisa. Perfect! Thank you for calling, Lucille. Have a great day! You too, Margaret! Bye. Bye!
